source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.228
purpose: Records the necessary conditions, quantifier/regularity/object/limit/normalization conventions, the core double-count boundaries, the author-unexpanded or open ranges, and the concrete source-notation points. Locations are 1-based TeX lines. Literal phenomena are reported; no correctness judgement is made and no formula is repaired.

necessary_conditions.condition: Base ring A is an integral Banach ring (unitary, commutative, submultiplicative norm, complete).
necessary_conditions.note: Integrality is required from section 2.4 onward (line 706) because the generic point and the Zariski-dense locus must exist.

necessary_conditions.condition: L is semi-ample on X for the definition of PSH(X,L) and for FS^tau(L) to be non-empty.
necessary_conditions.note: Line 647: FS^tau(L) non-empty iff L is semi-ample.

necessary_conditions.condition: X/A projective (and finite type) when compactness, Stone-Weierstrass density, or uniform-limit closure of PSH is used.
necessary_conditions.note: Density of DFS(X) assumes X/A projective (line 668); prop psh item 7 assumes X/A proper (line 730); prop at 737 assumes X/A proper.

necessary_conditions.condition: X -> D^* is a degeneration of complex manifolds, i.e. X smooth and pi a submersion, AND meromorphic at 0: there exists a normal complex analytic X-bar over D restricting to X over D^*.
For the hybrid construction, the degeneration is quasi-projective with a relatively algebraic embedding in P^N x D^* whose equations have meromorphic singularity at t=0.
k is a non-trivially valued field, Archimedean or not, for the hybrid field k^hyb.
necessary_conditions.note: Line 766 uses log|k^times| containing Z after scaling.

necessary_conditions.condition: For the hybrid ring A_r, r is fixed in (0,1) and the t-adic absolute value on K = C((t)) is normalized by |t| = r.
Discretely-valued field sections assume K complete, discretely valued, equicharacteristic zero (so K is isomorphic to k((t)) with v = ord_0).
L is relatively AMPLE (not merely semi-ample) in the non-Archimedean-limit subsection 3.2 and in the KE section; L is AMPLE in the admissible-data section 4.4.
Flatness of X over A is required for the fiberwise Monge-Ampere total mass to be independent of x; without it the question of continuity is not even well posed at the mass level.
Semistable reduction over the disk is assumed in the Kaehler-Einstein theorem as stated.
Continuity of the hybrid metric is required to conclude semi-positivity from a continuous extension (prop psh cont), and cannot be dropped.
necessary_conditions.note: Sharpness explained at line 1178 and Remark 826-832.

objects.object: PSH(X,L) over an integral Banach ring
objects.characterization: smallest class of singular metrics containing m^{-1}log|s| for non-zero global sections of mL and closed under addition of constants, finite maxima and decreasing limits, subject to phi_x not identically -infinity for all Zariski-dense x.

objects.note: continuous psh metrics with uniform-convergence topology.

objects.object: hybrid ring A_r and hybrid circle C^hyb(r) = M(A_r)

objects.note: A hybrid metric is by definition a (singular or continuous) metric on L^hyb viewing X as an A_r-scheme; PSH(L^hyb) is the paper's PSH class in this special case.
three equivalent formulations; the third is a sup bound against a smooth reference on a normal model.
psi^NA defined on divisorial valuations from generic Lelong numbers and extended lsc; the theorem is cited, not proved.

objects.object: Family of Monge-Ampere measures over M(A)
Canonical model X_c and model metric phi_{K_{X_c/D}}
objects.note: relatively ample but not snc; uniqueness from the relative canonical ring.

objects.object: Multiplier ideal I(phi) and analytic singularities along J

quantifiers_regularity_limits.item: All decreasing limits are limits of NETS (not sequences) in the general Banach-ring statements, and the nets must satisfy the non-identity--minus-infinity condition on Zariski-dense fibers.
quantifiers_regularity_limits.note: Sequences appear only when explicitly stated, e.g. the appendix regularization.

quantifiers_regularity_limits.item: PSH is NOT stable under non-flat base change; the author deliberately excludes metrics identically -infinity on a fiber and says so.
The non-Archimedean fiber value is a LOWER SEMICONTINUOUS extension of a function defined on divisorial valuations; upper/lower semicontinuity is part of the theorem's content (theo ext phina).
The converse of theo psh hyb is local in the radius: it is stated only on X restricted to the punctured disk of radius r - eps for a given eps > 0, not on the whole punctured disk.
Continuity in theo cont MA is WEAK continuity of measures against every continuous f on X^hyb, not norm or total-variation convergence.

In the appendix, the conclusion of theo reg psh holds on an arbitrary relatively compact open Y' contained in Y, with approximants in PSH(Y',L); convergence is pointwise on Y' and is upgraded to uniform only on relatively compact subsets.
The regularization scaling is dyadic: 2^j phi_j has analytic singularities of the form I_{2^j}.
Continuity of the extension in prop psh cont is hypothesis, not conclusion; the conclusion is semi-positivity.
In prop Song the estimate is stated for a fixed strict transform component and for all eps > 0 with a constant C_eps depending on eps; the upper bound is uniform in t.
The theorem on M(Z) requires phi to be continuous with values in R union {-infinity}; slopes and their sum are part of the characterization, not derived a posteriori.

normalization_and_sign_conventions.item: Metrics are written additively: phi = -log||.||, and phi = m^{-1} log|s| for a section s of mL.
dd^c = (i/pi) d dbar, extended to Hermitian metrics and to singular psh metrics.
Hybrid norm on k: ||z||_hyb = max(1,|z|); A_r norm: ||f||_hyb = sum_n ||a_n||_hyb r^n.
log_r|t| = log|t| / log r, non-negative on the closed disk of radius r.
At t=0 the hybrid absolute value is r^{ord_0(f)}; for t not 0 it is r^{log|f(t)|/log|t|}.
The map lambda(t) = log r / log|t| sends the closed disk of radius r onto [0,1] and is the map on Berkovich spectra induced by C^hyb -> A_r.
Rescaling in the hybrid dictionary: phi_t = phi|X_t = (log|t|/log r) * phi|X^hyb_t, i.e. the rescaled absolute value on a nonzero fiber.
Generic Lelong numbers: b_E = ord_E(t), and psi^NA(v) = (log r / b_E) * nu_E(phi) with nu_E(phi) = sup{c : phi_a <= c phi_E + O(1)} - a.
phi^NA := phi_L + psi^NA, where phi_L is the model metric of a chosen nef model.
KE normalization: int_{X_t} e^{psi_t} omega_FS,t^n = (K_{X_t})^n, with omega_KE,t = omega_FS,t + dd^c psi_t and the equation (omega_FS,t + dd^c psi_t)^n = e^{psi_t} omega_FS,t^n.
The reduction to pure Fubini-Study uses that c/log r = log|f| for some non-zero f in A_r when c is rational; this is specific to hybrid rings and fails for Z (e.g. A = Z), as the author emphasises.
Dirac masses at divisorial valuations in the explicit model Monge-Ampere formula: MA = sum_E b_E (L_1...L_n . E) delta_{v_E}.

explicit_omitted_details.kind: Isotrivial equivariant adaptation; author explicitly omits the rest after the weight decomposition. Keep as support with omission, not another complete independent primary.

resolved_internal_deferrals.resolution: Hybrid-circle converse points to the main theorem actually present; clear composition is a short coordinate identity.
Main regularization sketch points to complete appendix 1643-1806, which is present and read.

abbreviated_application_with_named_exter.role: KE application cites Song estimates already stated at 1614-1626; do not relabel a short application proof as a missing core.

source_notation_points.observation: phi_(m,m0) is already defined with denominator 2(m+m0) at 1254, while 1289 writes an additional (m+m0)^(-1) before phi_(m,m0) in its decreasing-limit sentence. Preserve the source expressions; do not silently normalize one to the other.

The two continuous maps and density argument are formulated on CPSH, while the final 1312 sentence says they coincide on PSH. Keep this literal tail sentence as metadata; the selected theorem converse remains restricted to CPSH and shrinking.

The theorem states singularities of I_(2^j), while its final sequence uses phi_(2^j-m0,m0) and 1705 identifies phi_(m,m0) singularities with I_m. Preserve all three source statements and their relation; do not replace the specified ideal or manufacture the missing index reconciliation.
n is set to dim Y at 1674; the Hilbert norm uses omega^n at 1692, while later local estimates use omega^(n+1). Record the literal exponents without changing a dimension convention or proof.
The appendix writes Y triple-prime at 1710 and Y double-prime at 1769, while surrounding subsets are Y-prime, Y_c and Y_(c-prime). Keep as original subset-name observations; do not invent subsets.

The projective-space example writes a logarithm of a squared sum at 1053 and a maximum of absolute values without a log at 1058. Retain those literal expressions alongside the actual definitions and later lemma; do not rewrite them.

The model is described as a model of itself at 342 (the raw note incorrectly points to 340); 706 writes mathscr X(x) in a sentence otherwise using H(x). These are literal symbol observations, not missing proof material.

The introduction uses pluripolar while the later discussion explicitly uses non-pluripolar for the special point. Preserve both original locations; do not resolve their terminology by rewriting the text.

deliberate_non_actions: No TeX macro was changed, no missing hypothesis was inserted, and no endpoint or scaling was corrected.
No printed theorem, definition or page number was invented; all such fields are null because reader.pdf is unusable.

producer_core_double_count_boundaries.boundary: Introduction Theorem A (th:A, 168-173) and Theorem B (th:B, 196-202) are forward-only restatements of theo psh hyb (1163-1176) and THEO KE NEG (1508-1514). Count each main result ONCE, using the full statement in the body.
theo Favre intro (183-188) and theo cont MA (1457-1462) are the same cited statement of Favre; only one external attribution, and no additional credit for the reformulation.
theo psh2 (760-763) is declared a mere reformulation of theo psh1 (607-608); theo psh1 itself reduces to [BE, Th. 7.1] and Lemma prop homo. None of the three is an independent advanced core.

prop sum psh (1261-1287), the lemma on continuity of (.)^NA (1298-1307), and prop semic phina (1181-1202) are components of the proof of theo psh hyb; counting them separately would count the same mechanism twice.

The convex-to-maximum transfer Lemma prop homo (1000-1049) is one mechanism; its instantiations in prop homo sing (983-999), the Bergman/geodesic-ray example (1064-1107), and the KE reference metric (1579-1587) are applications, not separate cores.

The appendix theorem theo reg psh (1662-1806) is a separate theorem with its own proof, but it is the technical engine of theo psh hyb; it must be counted once, and its sub-results prop glob gen and prop som part must not be counted as additional cores.
The Kaehler-Einstein theorem and its corollary (1508-1527) use the same assembly plus external Song estimates; the corollary adds no proof and is explicitly a consequence of theo cont MA.
The density of DFS (theo at 668) and prop psh (722) are explicitly attributed to [BJtriv] arguments; they are context, not new cores.

The M(Z) classification (834-904) and the hybrid-circle identification (779-824) are two different worked examples over two different base rings; they must not be merged, and the hybrid-circle one is not advanced because half of it is deferred to the main theorem.

The 'constants come from log|f| over a hybrid ring, so pure FS suffices' device (rem pure, 964-975) is used both in the main theorem and in the admissible-data dictionary; it is one supporting observation, counted as context.

Standard coordinate/parameter facts (the homeomorphism tau of the hybrid circle, the fiberwise description of the hybrid space, the fiber-of-analytification homeomorphism) are input, not new cores, even where a short proof is given.
The generic-Lelong-number construction of phi^NA (1117-1129) is exposition of cited results ([BBJ], [Reb]); it must not be counted as an author construction separate from theo ext phina.

producer_author_unexpanded_or_open_range.content: Lemma: restriction of phi_I to an snc skeleton is integral piecewise-affine, and the asserted converse.
Proposition prop bc hyb: base-change diagram, described as a straightforward consequence of transitivity of base change.
Proposition prop.FS: closure properties of FS^tau, called straightforward consequences of the definition.

The image of rho_r restricted to CPSH is expected to be the continuous subharmonic functions on the punctured disk extending continuously to the boundary with finite Lelong number at 0. This is NOT proved.
The converse direction of the hybrid-circle proposition is not proved here; it is delegated to Theorem theo psh hyb.
rho_r o rho_{r',r} equals restriction up to scaling: 'clear from the constructions'.

Favre's Question 1: does continuity of phi^NA force continuity of phi^hyb? The author reduces it to a uniform estimate phi_m - phi <= eps_m |log|t||^{-1} independent of t and says such a bound 'seems difficult to attain without a uniform estimate on the oscillation'.
Isotrivial positivity: after the S^1-weight decomposition 'the rest of the proof carries out without changes ... so we omit the details'.
Extending the Monge-Ampere operator on the finite-energy class over a general non-Archimedean field is stated to be unclear; known in the discretely-valued char 0 and trivially-valued cases.

Weak continuity of the fiberwise Monge-Ampere family over a general integral Banach ring; answered affirmatively only for hybrid rings, and expected for rings of integers (with [PoiDyn] giving a special case for Z).
The KE theorem's proof is three sentences and ends with an explicit qed instead of a proof environment; the substantive estimate is deferred to [Song, Cor. 4.1, Lem. 4.2].

The main theorem's proof says it will 'roughly' apply the same idea as the cited work, that the regularization is standard and due to Demailly, and that technical details are referred to the appendix.
The corollary on weak convergence of KE measures was proved directly in [PS, Th. A]; here it is recovered as a consequence.
The condition phi_x not identically -infinity on Zariski-dense points may be too strong in general; the author notes trivially-valued P^2 contains pluripolar Zariski-dense points.

owner_normal_conventions_not_author_gaps.reason: The reciprocal powers convert function values and norms between opposite rescaling directions. The explicit loose phi_t identity states the fibers involved; this is a normalization convention, not a gap inferred merely from reciprocals. The 949 raw note duplicates 948.

Normalized ord_E and negative-log absolute-value conventions have different scale factors. Preserve the quoted factors when assembling; a scale comparison alone is not proof of a defect or absent author material.

Maxima of log norms and minima of vanishing orders are linked by the valuation/sign convention. A raw min-versus-max difference alone is not a source gap; retain the exact generic-Lelong/model-metric formulas as needed context without independently certifying their equality.
R/disk base labels and placement of the relative-base subscript must be retained literally. They do not indicate a missing canonical-model construction.
Delimiter sizing and the unmatched display parenthesis are typography observations; they do not remove the specified maps or their author proof.
A shortened phi symbol in an explanatory paragraph is not by itself an author-proof omission.
Hybrid coefficient norm and absorption of rational constants into pure FS metrics are intentional definitions/constructions, not defects.
The discontinuous special-point example is an intentional scope boundary; unnamed diagram arrows are ordinary layout. Neither should be presented as missing author content.
